1.explanation:
• The core of the bug lives in needs-parens.js: the `needsParens` function is responsible for deciding when to preserve or drop surrounding parentheses on expressions. It currently doesn’t recognize JSDoc annotations like `@satisfies` as requiring parentheses, so it strips them off.

• The helper in is-type-cast-comment.js, `isTypeCastComment`, is used by `needsParens` to detect block comments that carry type information. It only looks for `@type`, not `@satisfies`, so JSDoc patterns beyond `@type` aren’t detected and parentheses aren’t preserved.

To fix the bug, `isTypeCastComment` should be extended (or a new utility added) to recognize `@satisfies` (and potentially other JSDoc tags) as type–annotation comments, and then `needsParens` will preserve the parentheses as intended.

2.explanation: The core of this bug is that Prettier only recognizes comments containing “@type” as type-cast annotations. In needs-parens.js, the function needsParens uses a helper (isTypeCastComment) to detect JSDoc type casts and preserve the surrounding parentheses. However, isTypeCastComment only tests for /@type\b/, so it doesn’t pick up other JSDoc tags like @satisfies. As a result, needsParens returns false and Prettier strips the parentheses around the object. To fix this, isTypeCastComment must be extended (or a new predicate added) to detect @satisfies (and similar tags), allowing needsParens to keep the parens intact.
